newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Venezuela's Petkoff sees 7.0 pct GDP growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Petkoff sees 7.0 pct GDP growth in '97.

text.p: Venezuelan Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said Thursday he expected gross domestic product growth next year, including the petroleum sector, to be near 7.0 percent.

Petkoff told reporters in Brasilia he also expected the federal government to post a surplus of 0.5 percent of gross domestic product by the end of 1996 versus a deficit in 1995 of 8.0 percent of GDP.
"Next year, we expect four percent GDP growth in the non-petroleum economy. With petrol, it will be near 7.0 percent," he said.

Petkoff, in Brazil for two days, said the economy would contract this year by an estimated 3.0-4.0 percent, but that the contraction would have been as much as 8.0 percent if Caracas had not adopted its economic adjustment program in April.
He said the government's fiscal target was to cut its deficit to 2.0 percent of GDP this year from 1995's 8.0 percent.
"But we will end the year with a small surplus of 0.5 percent," he said.
